I rated the ten below at 55% or higher. I dropped the dead-edge hypotheses (edge 2 or 4 edits conditioned on edge 0 being none) because they follow from the graph structure alone. The naive reasoning I expect other models to fall for is that an edit's average effect is the same as its interaction. In fact, replacing `none` is nearly always the largest gain, and removing a strong op is the largest loss. Parallel convs and direct skips also show diminishing returns that a "more capacity is better" view misses.
